title: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Opens to Rs 18 Crore in India, Smashing His Own Record for Biggest Debut
excerpt: The first film ever shot entirely on IMAX cameras earned nearly Rs 21 crore gross on its opening day, surpassing Oppenheimer's Rs 14 crore net debut by a wide margin.
body:
• The Odyssey earned an estimated Rs 17.5–18.5 crore net (Rs 20.65–21.83 crore gross) on its opening day in India, the biggest debut ever for a Christopher Nolan film.
  • It comfortably surpassed Oppenheimer's Rs 14 crore net opening day and is the biggest Hollywood opening in India in 2026 by a wide margin.
  • IMAX 2D screenings recorded morning occupancy of 74 percent, rising to 82 percent for evening shows, driven by the film's distinction as the first shot entirely on 70mm IMAX cameras.
  • The film released across 2,500+ screens in India, compared to Oppenheimer's 1,923-screen debut.

Nolan's Biggest Indian Opening

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Mzw2ttJD2qQ

Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey opened to a commanding Rs 17.5–18.5 crore net at the Indian box office on Friday, according to early trade estimates from Koimoi and Sacnilk, registering the director's biggest opening day in the country and the largest debut for a Hollywood film in India this year.

The figure translates to roughly Rs 20.65–21.83 crore in gross terms. It surpassed Nolan's own record set by Oppenheimer, which opened to Rs 14 crore net (Rs 17.77 crore gross) in 2023. The next-closest Hollywood release in 2026, The Devil Wears Prada sequel, opened at just Rs 5.5 crore, making The Odyssey's lead enormous.

"It surpassed Nolan's own record set by <em>Oppenheimer</em>, which opened to Rs 14 crore net (Rs 17.77 crore gross) in 2023."

IMAX Drove the Numbers

Premium format screenings were the dominant force behind the opening. The Odyssey is the first feature film ever shot entirely on 70mm IMAX cameras, and Indian audiences responded with premium-format occupancy rates that outpaced every recent Hollywood release.

IMAX 2D morning shows recorded 74 percent occupancy, rising to 75 percent in the afternoon and hitting 82 percent in evening screenings. The 4DX format started at 42 percent occupancy and peaked at 52 percent in afternoons. Across India's 34 IMAX screens, approximately 91,000 tickets had been sold in advance, generating Rs 9.5 crore in gross ticket sales from IMAX alone.

The film released across more than 2,500 screens in India — a 30 percent increase over Oppenheimer's 1,923-screen count — reflecting the wider reach and higher buzz generated by Nolan's Mumbai promotional visit with stars Tom Holland and Matt Damon.

India's Growing Role in Hollywood Calculations

India has steadily grown as a priority market for major Hollywood releases, and The Odyssey's performance cements that trajectory. The film's advance booking of approximately 140,000 tickets in the top two national chains (PVR Inox and Cinepolis) fell below Oppenheimer's 200,000 in raw ticket count, but higher ticket prices — driven by IMAX and premium surcharges — pushed the opening-day collection higher in rupee terms.

"Oppenheimer opened to Rs 17.77 crore gross. The Odyssey should aim to get close to Rs 20 crore gross."

— Pinkvilla box office forecast, published ahead of release

The film also benefits from Indian-origin British actor Himesh Patel's role in the ensemble, adding a diaspora connection to a film already commanding global attention.

Strong Weekend Expected

With overwhelmingly positive critical reception and strong initial audience reactions, trade analysts expect The Odyssey to have a robust opening weekend. Early word of mouth from premiere screenings was enthusiastic. If Saturday and Sunday collections maintain the trajectory, the film could cross Rs 55–60 crore net by the end of its opening weekend, potentially making it one of the top five Hollywood openers of all time in India.
